glance.finding: mask course-media-http2-reset (console) added since 17.0.0-rc.1: it hid 1 value in this run
glance.detail: reason: Chromium streams a course video or audio file in byte ranges and cancels the ranges it no longer wants when the page settles or moves on; over HTTP/2 to the reference course on Netlify (reference-course.netlify.app) a cancelled or reset stream is sometimes logged as "Failed to load resource: net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR" for the file. Whether a stream is cut while the page is watched is the transport's timing, not the release's: the A/A of 2026-10-23 (noise report 2026-10-23T02-01-40Z, run 39884229709, 17.0.0 on both sides, same digests) logged it for {{course}}/topic-07-reference/note-1/img/video.mov on reference:note on side b only, its only difference, after four clean A/A runs (2026-10-19 to 2026-10-22). The release does not serve the course: the reader only puts the video element on the page, and the fixture course the forecast judges is plain HTTP/1.1 on localhost, where this error cannot occur. The console engine compares a page's messages as a set, so the entry is dropped. Only this one transport error, only on media files under the course origin, is dropped: a 404 or 500 on the same file (the "server responded with a status of" message), any other net:: error, the same error on the reader's own origin or another host, and every other console message still compare; the media request itself still compares on the network artefact (media-range-status). Blind spot: a course host that starts failing media streams over HTTP/2 is invisible on the console artefact.
